definition: Quandary means a perplexed, unresolvable state.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word quandary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know quandary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The judging invitation put Chef Luis in a quandary: accept it, and his own mole recipe was out of the running.
Indecision is the everyday wobble between menu items; a quandary goes further - a knot where every option costs something real.
Paralysis is the far end: in a quandary you still weigh your options, but in decision paralysis the weighing never ends and no choice ever comes.

A dilemma is the two-horned choice itself — the classic word for a fork with exactly two options, both of them painful. A quandary is the state that such a choice puts you in: stuck, puzzled, circling. You face a dilemma; you are in a quandary.

A predicament is any tight spot — a stalled car, an overdrawn account — whether or not a choice is involved at all. A quandary is specifically a chooser's trap: real options sit in front of you, each one costing something, and no rule sorts them.
knowing exactly what to do next
the knot untied - a decision actually made

Quandary surfaces in English around 1580 with no certain parent. The best guess ties it to Latin quando, 'when,' as a bit of university slang for being stuck on a question. Because the origin itself is unsettled, there is no root here to reuse - the whole word is the unit.
Quandary means a perplexed, unresolvable state.
The tide table put the kayak guide in a quandary: paddle back against the rising wind with a tired group, or wait out the chop and miss the harbor gate before it locked for the night.
Quandary names the guide's state exactly: two real options, each carrying a cost she cannot wish away, and no rule that sorts them.
A predicament needs only trouble; a quandary needs a choice that refuses to sort itself out - and she is in one until the wind or the clock decides for her.
Quandary names the stuck, puzzled state you are in when no option comes out clean - you are in a quandary, never merely near one.
Dilemma names the two-horned choice itself; predicament is any tight spot, choice or no choice.
Ambiguity (this unit) lives in the wording; a quandary lives in you.

When the letter from the coastal village arrived, curator Dana Okafor read it three times and then sat very still.
It asked, politely, for the return of a carved orca mask -- the centerpiece of her museum's hall, and by every record honestly purchased eighty years ago.

Her quandary occupied the rest of the season: return the mask and hollow out the hall that funded the education wing, keep it and betray what the exhibit claimed to honor, or loan it and satisfy no one.
Colleagues offered rules -- follow the law, follow the donors, follow your conscience -- and every rule pointed a different way.
It was not that Dana couldn't decide quickly; it was that each available decision cost something she was hired to protect.
